page: Microsoft Azure NV12ads_V710_v5 is a virtualized server instance powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD processor with 12 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 5.33 GB of RAM per core. The hardware configuration includes a fractional GPU allocation of 0.5 V710 GPU with 11 GB of dedicated VRAM, alongside 825 GB of local storage. The instance is also Premium Storage capable.

This server family utilizes fractional GPU partitioning, which provides a qualitative cost-efficiency advantage for workloads that require GPU acceleration but do not scale to or justify the cost of a full, dedicated physical GPU. By provisioning half of a V710 GPU, users can run graphics-intensive or accelerated compute tasks with a lower resource overhead. However, a potential tradeoff is the shared nature of the physical GPU component and the lack of complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The NV12ads_V710_v5 is designed for workloads such as virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI), lightweight 3D rendering, entry-level machine learning inference, and general-purpose applications that benefit from hardware acceleration. The combination of 12 vCPUs, 64.0 GB of RAM, and local storage makes it suitable for multi-user environments and database-backed applications requiring moderate graphical or parallel processing capabilities.
